column1: What do latitude \(\varphi\) and longitude \(\lambda\) measure?
column2: Latitude: angle north (+) or south (-) of the equator. Longitude: angle east (+) or west (-) of the Greenwich meridian.

Why prefer haversine over the law of cosines for short distances?

Why does the shortest New York to London route curve north on a flat map?
column2: A degree of longitude is shorter near the poles. The great circle does its east-west travel at high latitude. Mercator does not draw great circles straight.

Mercator length scale and area scale at latitude \(\varphi\)
Why does Greenland look as big as Africa on Mercator?
column2: At about 72 degrees N the area factor is \(\sec^2 72^\circ \approx 10.5\). Africa is 14 times bigger but sits near the equator, where the factor is about 1.

column1: Equirectangular projection formulas and its flaw
column2: \(x = R\lambda,\ y = R\varphi\). Even latitude spacing, but east-west is stretched by \(\sec\varphi\) and north-south is not. Shapes squash.

column1: What does a Tissot circle show?
column2: A small circle of fixed ground size drawn on a map. Its distortion shows how the projection stretches area and shape at that spot.
